titleEn: Can't See Grandma? Stop and Call!

pages.text: "I'll go first!" Yuki ran ahead on the mountain path. In gray layered clothes, Grandma walked slowly with a mushroom basket. "Only go where I can see you."
"I'll find mushrooms first!" Yuki ran farther over rustling leaves. The footsteps behind were no longer heard.
Yuki looked back. No Grandma on the path. Thick trees stood everywhere, and Yuki could not tell which way they had come. "Grandma...?" Both hands clasped tightly at their chest.
"Only where I can see you." Yuki repeated the morning words aloud and stayed right there, without another step. A deep breath filled their chest, then slowly left.
"Grandma! Grandma!" Yuki cupped their hands and called loudly. Leaves swallowed the sound, making it fade. Brown dog Momo sat close beside Yuki and whined.
Without moving one step, Yuki called again. "Grandma!" A piece of gray clothing appeared between the trees. "There she is!"
Grandma strode over with the basket. Yuki ran into her sleeves. "Can't See Grandma? Stop and Call!"
"You stayed still and called, so I found you quickly." Grandma held Yuki's hand tight. Together, they picked mushrooms beneath the leaves.

Days later, Yuki ran ahead and looked back again. The path was quiet. Yuki stopped right there and tied the scarf knot tightly. "One, stop if I can't see her! Two, call loudly! Three, wait until she comes!"
Grandma gently rubbed her cheek against Yuki's. Staying still and calling brought a grown-up to find them. Yuki gripped her hand tighter. "Can't See Grandma? Stop and Call!"
